exposure: Maternal sero-miR-155 levels (at first, second, and third trimesters)
cohort: Pregnant women, including those with preeclampsia and healthy controls, totaling 525 for the case-control and 411 for the longitudinal cohort study.
finding: High maternal sero-miR-155 levels are significantly elevated in preeclampsia and are associated with more severe clinical manifestations, identifying a distinct subtype of preeclampsia.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken at first, second, and third trimesters of pregnancy.
